_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 1 Mathematics unit lecture film, What Comes Next. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson's own three-part lecture (patterns that repeat; jump patterns; the equals sign) with the lesson's own growing-shape step between the last two, and they use the lesson's own numbers: its orange-and-teal bead row, its purple-gold-gold unit, its 2 4 6 8 10 and 10 9 8 7 6 jump patterns, its pattern-of-two growing shapes (2, 4, 6, 8) and its first balance, 4 + 2 = ? + 3.
title: What Comes Next
subtitle: Grade 1 Mathematics
objectives: Use familiar language to describe sequences of objects.
Count on in ones, twos or tens, and count back in ones and tens, starting from any number (from 0 to 20).
Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers (where the answer is from 0 to 20).

beats.say: Some things happen again and again, in the same order.
That is a pattern. Spot the part that repeats, and you can say what comes next.
Look at these beads. Orange, teal, orange, teal, orange.
Say the colours out loud, and let your voice run on past the end.
Your voice wants to say teal next. Your voice is right.
Two colours can take turns, and that is a pattern too. It repeats the same part over and over.
So start at the beginning every time, and let the words carry you on.
Every pattern has one small part that repeats.
Purple, gold, gold. Then purple, gold, gold again.
Three beads repeat. You can draw a line after every three.
Now one bead is missing. Look at the bead before the hole.
The part that repeats tells you exactly what belongs there.
Numbers make patterns too. Two, four, six, eight, ten.
Each number is two more than the one before it.
That is a jump pattern, and the jump is the same every time.
A jump can go backwards too. Ten, nine, eight, seven, six.
Find the jump first. Then you can fill any hole in the line.
Some patterns grow. Each one adds a new row of two shapes.
Two shapes, then four, then six. Count them every time.

at.counts: Two shapes, then four, then six

beats.say: The counts jump up by two, just like the numbers did.
So pattern four has eight shapes. Six, and two more.
A growing pattern gets bigger by the same amount each time.
The equals sign means the same amount on both sides.
It does not mean here comes the answer.
Three add something makes seven. How many are missing?
Count on from three: four, five, six, seven. That is four.
Now a scale. Four add two on one side, three on the other.
Add three more, and it sits level. Both sides make six.
A pattern has a part that repeats. Find it and carry on.
A jump pattern goes up or down by the same amount.
And equals means the same on both sides. Now go and try it.
